descs.t: Egypt is moving toward sending troops to Saudi Arabia to help defend against attacks by the Iran-backed Houthis, and three European powers have joined the defense of the kingdom after a deadly attack. In Yemen, the Houthis attacked a besieged city the UN says is at grave risk. We walk through who is joining and what each one brings.

Egypt and three European powers are lining up to defend Saudi Arabia against the Iran-backed Houthis after a deadly attack. The Houthis are also pressing a besieged Yemeni city the UN says is at grave risk. We look at what this coalition means for the Houthis and for Iran's regime.

Iran's Houthi proxy is attacking Saudi Arabia and a besieged city in Yemen, and now Egypt and three European powers are moving to stop it. Tehran built this militia to spread its war. We look at whether that strategy is starting to backfire on the regime.

intro.plain: Big shift in the Gulf today. Egypt is moving toward sending troops to Saudi Arabia to help defend it against attacks by the Iran-backed Houthis. Three European powers have joined the defense after a deadly attack. And in Yemen, the UN says a besieged city is at grave risk. Chat, would Egyptian troops make a difference?
intro.mid: Egypt is moving toward putting troops in Saudi Arabia, and three European powers are already in, all to defend against Iran's Houthis after a deadly attack. That is a coalition forming in real time. The question is what it does to Tehran's plans. Chat, does this put real pressure on the regime?
intro.bold: Iran's regime armed the Houthis to set the region on fire, and now it is getting a coalition in return. Egypt is moving to send troops to Saudi Arabia, and three European powers have joined its defense. Chat, is the Islamic Republic's proxy strategy finally backfiring?

hook.plain: Egypt is moving toward sending troops to Saudi Arabia, and three European powers have already joined its defense. Here is who is in, and why.
hook.mid: A deadly Houthi attack has pulled Egypt and Europe into Saudi Arabia's defense. Here is what this coalition means for Iran's proxies.
hook.bold: Iran's Houthis attacked Saudi Arabia, and now Egypt and three European powers are lining up against them. Here is how Tehran's proxy war is turning on it.

descs.t: Italy is set to deploy 500 soldiers to Milan after weekend riots, Politico reports, with The Guardian and Le Monde also covering it. Reuters reports the government will also boost police arrest powers. We walk through what Italy is sending and why.

Italy is answering the Milan riots with soldiers and stronger arrest powers for police. It is a hard response to a weekend of violence. We go through what the deployment of 500 soldiers involves and what the new powers mean.

Italy is sending 500 soldiers into Milan after masked gangs trashed the city, according to reports, and police are getting more power to arrest. Italy is not waiting for things to get worse. We break down the crackdown.

intro.plain: Let's go to Italy. After weekend riots in Milan, Italy is set to deploy 500 soldiers to the city, and the government says it will boost police arrest powers too. That is a serious response. Question for the chat: is sending soldiers into a city the right answer to riots?
intro.mid: Italy is not messing around. After the Milan riots, it is sending 500 soldiers to the city and giving police more power to arrest people. Compare that with how other governments handle this. Chat, which approach actually works, soldiers on the street or something else?
intro.bold: Masked gangs trashed parts of Milan over the weekend, according to reports, and Italy's answer is 500 soldiers and stronger arrest powers for police. That is a government drawing a line. Chat, tell me: should more countries do exactly this?

hook.plain: Italy is set to deploy 500 soldiers to Milan after a weekend of riots. Here is what the government is doing and why.
hook.mid: 500 soldiers for one city. Italy's answer to the Milan riots is the army plus new arrest powers. Here is what that means.
hook.bold: Masked gangs hit Milan, and Italy is sending in the army. Here is how one government decided enough was enough.

descs.t: Meta has told a Brazilian court that it treats the campaigns of Lula and Bolsonaro equally, as Brazil heads into its final election vote. Lula supporters have protested against Meta, accusing it of electoral interference. We walk through what Meta told the court and what each side is claiming.

Lula is challenging Flavio Bolsonaro to make his financial records public while his supporters accuse Meta of electoral interference. Meta says it treats both campaigns equally. We look at what is at stake in Brazil's final vote and in the role of big platforms in elections.

Lula says Brazil's sovereignty is at stake in this final election, and his supporters are aiming that fight at Meta. Meta insists to a Brazilian court that it treats Lula and Bolsonaro the same. We break down the clash and what it means for who shapes Brazil's vote.

intro.plain: Meta has just told a Brazilian court that it treats the Lula and Bolsonaro campaigns equally. That comes after Lula supporters protested against Meta, accusing it of electoral interference, with Brazil heading into its final election vote. So the question for chat: do you believe a platform like Meta can stay neutral in an election this close?
intro.mid: Brazil's final election fight has a new front, and it is Meta. The company told a court it treats Lula and Bolsonaro equally, while Lula's supporters protest what they call electoral interference. And Lula is daring Flavio Bolsonaro to make his financial records public. Chat, who do you think is really trying to shape this vote?
intro.bold: Lula says Brazil's sovereignty is on the line in this final election, and his side has picked a target: Meta. His supporters are protesting what they call electoral interference, and Meta is telling a court it treats both campaigns equally. Chat, tell me straight: is this about protecting Brazil, or about controlling what voters see?

hook.plain: Meta has told a Brazilian court it treats Lula and Bolsonaro equally. Here is why it had to say that, and what each side claims.
hook.mid: Lula's supporters are protesting Meta for electoral interference. Meta says it is neutral. Here is the fight shaping Brazil's final vote.
hook.bold: Lula says Brazil's sovereignty is at stake, and his side is pointing at Meta. Here is what the platform told the court, and why it matters.

descs.t: President Trump and Vice President JD Vance have announced a $25 million fraud whistleblower incentive program. It is meant to encourage the public to report alleged fraud. We walk through what was announced and what it asks of the public.

Trump and JD Vance are putting $25 million behind a whistleblower program to get the public reporting alleged fraud. We look at what the program promises and the stakes for anyone tempted to cheat the system.

Trump and Vance are offering a $25 million incentive to people who help expose fraud. The message is simple: report it and the program rewards you. We break down the announcement and what it means for those who thought nobody was watching.

intro.plain: Just announced: President Trump and Vice President JD Vance are launching a $25 million fraud whistleblower incentive program, meant to encourage the public to report alleged fraud. Chat, would a reward like this make you more likely to report fraud you saw?
intro.mid: Trump and JD Vance put $25 million behind a whistleblower program on fraud. The idea is to turn ordinary people into the eyes and ears against fraud. Chat, do you think paying whistleblowers works, or does it invite false reports?
intro.bold: $25 million to go after fraud. Trump and Vance just announced a whistleblower incentive program, and the message to anyone cheating the system is clear: the public is now watching. Chat, where should they look first?

hook.plain: Trump and JD Vance have announced a $25 million fraud whistleblower program. Here is what it is and who it asks to speak up.
hook.mid: Trump and Vance are putting $25 million behind people who report fraud. Here is what they announced and what it could change.
hook.bold: $25 million, aimed at fraud, and the public is now the watchdog. Here is what Trump and Vance just launched.

descs.t: Russia has proposed a meeting between Trump, Xi and Putin in China next month, as US envoy Witkoff prepares to meet Putin. The Washington Post, Reuters and NBC News report Trump pressing Kyiv to settle while Zelenskyy calls for three way talks. This walks through what each side is offering and where the talks stand.

Russia wants Trump and Xi at the same table with Putin in China, and Ukraine is not in that picture. US ties with Kyiv have hit a new low as Trump eases up on Moscow and Witkoff heads to Putin. Here is what the summit offer means for the war and for Zelenskyy.

Putin is inviting Trump to China while Ukraine is told to settle. With the talks and the front both at an impasse, the question is who pays for a deal made over Kyiv's head. This breaks down the summit offer, the Oslo meeting and the pressure on Zelenskyy.

intro.plain: Russia has proposed a meeting between Trump, Xi and Putin in China next month. At the same time Witkoff is set to meet Putin, Trump is pressing Kyiv to settle, and Zelenskyy is asking for three way talks with Putin and Trump. The talks and the battlefield are both stuck. Chat, should Ukraine have a seat at any meeting about its own war?
intro.mid: Putin wants Trump and Xi in China next month, and Ukraine is not on that guest list. US ties with Kyiv are at a new low, Trump is easing up on Russia, and Witkoff is headed to Putin. Chat, is this the road to peace or a deal made over Ukraine's head?
intro.bold: Putin just invited Trump to sit down with him and Xi in China, while Washington presses Kyiv to settle. Zelenskyy wants a seat at the table, and right now he does not have one. Chat, tell me straight: would you trust any deal Putin brokers in China?

hook.plain: Russia wants Trump, Xi and Putin together in China next month. Here is what is on the table, and where Ukraine stands.
hook.mid: US ties with Ukraine just hit a new low, and Russia is offering Trump a summit in China. Here is what that offer really changes.
hook.bold: Putin is inviting Trump to China while Kyiv is told to settle. In the next few minutes you will see who gains and who pays.

descs.t: Reports say Donald Trump nearly approved strikes on Iran, while Benjamin Netanyahu says he discussed eliminating the Iranian regime with him. The Jerusalem Post and CBS News carried the strike report, and Trump has also said he could leave Iran now while ruling out a nuclear weapon. Here is what each statement means.

Trump came close to approving strikes on Iran, and Netanyahu now says the two discussed eliminating the regime. At the same time Trump says he could leave Iran now, as long as Tehran never gets a nuclear weapon. This walks through the signals and what they mean for the Islamic Republic.

Netanyahu is talking openly about eliminating Iran's regime, and Trump nearly approved strikes. For the Islamic Republic the message is plain: no nuclear weapon, and the pressure is not letting up. This breaks down the reports and what pressure on Tehran looks like now.

intro.plain: Reports say Trump nearly approved strikes on Iran. Netanyahu says he discussed eliminating the Iranian regime with him. And Trump also says he could leave Iran now, but Iran will not get a nuclear weapon. Three signals in one day. Chat, which one do you think is the real plan?
intro.mid: Trump came close to signing off on Iran strikes, and Netanyahu is now saying out loud that he talked with Trump about eliminating the regime. Meanwhile Trump says he could walk away now, but no bomb for Tehran. Chat, is this pressure working, or are we hearing mixed signals?
intro.bold: Netanyahu says the Iranian regime should be eliminated, and he says he discussed it with Trump. Trump nearly approved strikes. This is the conversation so many Iranians have waited for. Chat, does the West finally have the will to finish this regime?

hook.plain: Trump nearly approved strikes on Iran, according to reports. Netanyahu says they discussed ending the regime. Here is what was said and what it means.
hook.mid: Strikes almost approved, an exit on the table, and no nuclear weapon for Tehran. Here is how Trump's three Iran signals fit together.
hook.bold: Netanyahu wants Iran's regime eliminated, and Trump nearly said yes to strikes. Here is why Tehran should be worried.

descs.t: France is facing violent unrest, and the Fact Check Team asks what is driving it. AP reports that social unrest is setting streets ablaze across Europe. This video walks through what is happening in France and why.

Rioters are bringing chaos to France, and the violence is part of wider social unrest across Europe, according to AP. Here is what is behind France's unrest, what the coverage shows, and what it means for the country.

France's streets are ablaze with rioting that Fox News describes as terror and chaos. With unrest spreading across Europe, this breaks down what is driving the violence and why it matters far beyond France.

intro.plain: France is dealing with violent unrest, and the question everyone is asking is what is driving it. AP reports the unrest is not only in France, it is setting streets ablaze across Europe too. Chat, what do you think is behind this?
intro.mid: Rioters are terrorizing parts of France right now, and it is part of a wider wave of street unrest across Europe. I want to get into what is actually driving it. Chat, is this about money, or something deeper?
intro.bold: France is in chaos. Rioters are on the streets, the violence is real, and unrest is spreading across Europe. Chat, how long before a European government loses control? Tell me what you are seeing.

hook.plain: France is facing violent unrest. Here is what is driving it, and where else in Europe it is spreading.
hook.mid: Rioters are bringing chaos to France, and Europe's streets are heating up with it. Here is what is behind it.
